title: Microsurge runway matrix by AZ and GPU family — forecast 2026
summary: 15-minute microsurge runway matrix and buffer targets computed per availability zone (AZ) and GPU family for the Hosted API fleet. Purpose: define operational prewarm and safe-pool sizing for short, high-intensity token bursts driven by chat and embedding traffic. Focus is on AZ-level rotation, fast fallback to quantized model variants, and prewarm slot allocation to minimize cold-start amplification during regional microspikes.
projections_methodology: We derived base tokens/sec and base QPS from 90th-percentile per-AZ telemetry (past 90 days) and synthetic microburst synthesis (Poisson sampling with 15min windows). For each AZ+GPU family: compute base steady-state throughput, measure historical 15min spike multiplier, define buffer target = base * spike_multiplier * safety_factor (1.2 unless otherwise noted). Convert tokens to QPS using observed median tokens/request per workload mix (chat=320t, embeddings=64t, rerank=180t). Add prewarm slots to cover ~T90 of cold-start impact (empirical model). Round pool sizes up to nearest alloc unit (4 GPUs).
decisions: 1) Set default safety_factor to 1.2 for consumer chat-heavy AZs; 1.35 for EU regions during upcoming marketing push. 2) Prioritize H100 pools for low-latency chat variants and A100 for mixed embedding+chat. 3) Reserve a 10% cross-AZ overflow capacity (fast-rotating safepool) to absorb node failures during microsurges. 4) Prewarm slots should be charged to burst budget and reconciled weekly with cost reports.
open_questions: Should we treat L4 pools as strictly inference-cache only or allow short-lived model loadups for very bursty customers?
Do we increase prewarm slots in eu-west1 for the GDPR compliance pilot that starts Apr 2026?
Validate whether the 1.2 safety_factor underestimates multi-tenant correlated spikes — run a 10k-sample stress sim?

notes: Operational playbook snippets: rotate prewarm ownership every 6 hours to distribute cost, autoscales trigger if 10-min rolling tokens/sec exceeds 80% buffer_target for two consecutive 15-min windows. Fallback policy: if AZ safepool depleted, route 30% of traffic to quantized variant (Q4) with warmup-in-flight; remaining 70% uses cross-AZ spillover prioritized by latency. Cost tracking: tag prewarm instances with 'burst-budget-v2' and reconcile against hosted-api burst ledger.
